name: InSite
question: Does sacral neuromodulation with InterStim produce higher 6-month therapeutic success than standard medical therapy in adults with overactive bladder who have failed an anticholinergic?

arms.label: standard medical therapy with antimuscarinic drugs

design.population: Adults with bothersome overactive bladder (urge incontinence of at least 2 leaks per 72 hours and/or at least 8 voids per day) who had failed at least one anticholinergic and had at least one not yet tried; 93% were women and mean age was 58.
design.description: Multicenter, open-label randomized superiority trial with nonrandomized implanted cohort
design.locator: abstract; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00547378 (design, arms, outcome definitions)

verdictNote: SNM success exceeded medical therapy at 6 months; randomized comparison was open-label and lasted 6 months.
takeaway: In adults with refractory overactive bladder, sacral neuromodulation (InterStim) achieved higher 6-month therapeutic success than standard medication (61% versus 42%, intention to treat), with greater quality-of-life gains; device-related adverse events occurred in 18 of 59 implanted participants (30.5%).

reports.label: 6-month randomized report
reports.citation: Siegel S, Noblett K, Mangel J, et al. Results of a prospective, randomized, multicenter study evaluating sacral neuromodulation with InterStim therapy compared to standard medical therapy at 6-months in subjects with mild symptoms of overactive bladder. *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2015;34(3):224-230.

results.measure: 6-month OAB therapeutic success, intention to treat; risk difference in percentage points (SNM minus medical therapy)
results.note: Success was at least 50% improvement in average leaks per day (urge incontinence) or in voids per day, or fewer than 8 voids per day (urgency-frequency). The prespecified hypothesis was a greater response rate with SNM; the difference is derived by subtraction.

results.measure: 6-month OAB therapeutic success, as-treated analysis; risk difference in percentage points (SNM minus medical therapy)
Improved or greatly improved urinary symptom interference score at 6 months
results.note: The abstract reports significantly greater quality-of-life improvement with SNM on all measures (all P<0.001); denominators are not given.

harms.label: Adverse events related to the assigned treatment
harms.note: The neuromodulation safety denominator is participants with a lead implant, not all 70 randomized to neuromodulation.

delivery.label: Enrollment and randomization
delivery.value: Medication washout and baseline diary, then 1:1 randomization; 70 to SNM and 77 to medical therapy at 38 centers.

delivery.label: Test stimulation before implant
delivery.value: Subjects in each group went through test stimulation and received a full system implant if it was successful.

delivery.label: Crossover after the randomized comparison
delivery.value: After the month 6 visit, subjects in the medical therapy group could choose test stimulation and, if successful, a full system implant.

reports.label: Adverse events and interventions to 12 months
reports.citation: Noblett K, Benson K, Kreder K. Detailed analysis of adverse events and surgical interventions in a large prospective trial of sacral neuromodulation therapy for overactive bladder patients. *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2017;36(4):1136-1139.

harms.label: Device-related adverse events through 12 months
harms.note: Only one was serious; 56% of the events occurred between implant and 3 months, and a Clinical Events Committee adjudicated them.

harms.label: Implant site pain
harms.note: Of 26 pain events, 13 required surgical intervention and 2 ended in explant.

harms.label: Implant site infection
harms.note: Ten subjects had 13 surgical site infection events (including one cellulitis); 5 resolved with antibiotics and 8 required explantation.

harms.label: Surgical intervention through 12 months
harms.note: Reasons: pain at the surgical site (4%), lack or loss of efficacy (4%) and infection (3%); most interventions were revision or replacement.

reports.label: 5-year follow-up of implanted subjects
reports.citation: Siegel S, Noblett K, Mangel J, et al. Five-year followup results of a prospective, multicenter study of patients with overactive bladder treated with sacral neuromodulation. *J Urol.* 2018;199(1):229-236.
reports.followUp: 5 years after implant; 340 completed test stimulation and 272 were implanted

results.measure: 5-year therapeutic success among 183 of 272 implanted subjects, modified completers analysis (95% CI 60–74%)
results.note: Success was at least 50% improvement in leaks or voids per day, or fewer than 8 voids per day. Single-arm analysis of implanted subjects.

results.measure: 5-year therapeutic success among 150 of 272 implanted subjects, completers analysis (95% CI 76–88%)
Five-year completers mean reduction; baseline mean 3.1 leaks per day in 202 subjects with urge incontinence at baseline
Five-year completers mean reduction; baseline mean 12.6 voids per day in 189 subjects with urgency-frequency at baseline

results.endpoint: Tined lead adverse events requiring surgery
results.measure: Cumulative 5-year probability of tined lead related adverse events requiring surgery or revision, all implanted subjects; prespecified upper 95% confidence bound below 0.33
results.note: Read from the ClinicalTrials.gov results record, not from the published paper.

delivery.label: Implantation after test stimulation
delivery.value: 272 of 340 subjects who completed test stimulation received an implant; 91% were women and mean age was 57.
